newsitem.title: USA: Fire turns Kentucky apartments into deadly furnace.
newsitem.headline: Fire turns Kentucky apartments into deadly furnace.

text.p: An early morning fire Tuesday turned the century-old Victory Apartments into a deadly "furnace" for a still-unknown number of victims, police said.
Firefighters continued to pour water on the burning embers of the eight-unit apartment house that was home to mostly young residents, a post office and a real estate office.
"When it burned it was like a furnace with everything going up the chimney," Kentucky State Police Trooper Bryan Pitney said.
"We do know that there were fatalities but we don't know how many, and we won't know until the building cools and we can get in there," he said.

Pitney said a forensic anthropologist had been called in to try to identify what will likely be barely recogniseable remains of the unknown number of victims. Specially trained dogs may be used to sift through the incinerated remains.

Four of the eight small apartments in the building were rented out, but there may have been guests staying there overnight. "These were inexpensive apartments for kids starting out on their own," Pitney said.
Two unsupported brick walls teetered precariously over the still-hot ashes of the 1903-era wooden structure, making it impossible for anyone to enter safely, he said.
Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms experts would assess whether the fire started accidentally or was a case of arson.

The blaze on Earlington's Main Street caused the top floors of the building to collapse and melted nearby telephone wires, cutting off telephone service to the town of 1,800 about 140 miles southwest of Louisville.
